name: Doxofylline
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

overview.mechanism: Doxofylline is a xanthine that differs from theophylline by a dioxolane group at position 7. Unlike theophylline, it has no significant effect on the known phosphodiesterase isoforms and no significant adenosine receptor antagonism; an interaction with beta-2 adrenoceptors has been described. It has bronchodilator and anti-inflammatory effects.
uses: Airway obstruction in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), as an alternative to theophylline

In a meta-analysis of 20 trials in COPD (820 patients) it improved FEV1, with gastrointestinal upset and headache as the more frequent adverse events; fewer drug interactions than theophylline are reported

sources.citation: Matera, M. G., Page, C., & Cazzola, M. (2017). Doxofylline is not just another theophylline! International Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, 12, 3487–3493.
